newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Few changes seen in EU 1997/98 farm price package.
newsitem.headline: Few changes seen in EU 1997/98 farm price package.

text.p: European Commission price proposals for 1997/98 (July/June), expected early February, are again likely to be fairly modest, Commission officials said.
Farm support prices and compensation payments look set to remain unchanged, although Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler may again try to cut monthly increases in grain storage payments.
A fresh bid may be made to cut monthly sugar storage refunds.
"The package is likely to be very small...mainly a roll-over of existing measures," a Commission official said.
The aim is to consolidate the 1992 reform of the Common Agricultural Policy (CAP) and take account of subsidy-cutting and market-opening measures under the world farm trade accord.
But ministers are again expected to resort to traditional tactics of trying to add "sweeteners" for their farmers and negotiations could again drag through until June.
However, the margin for manoeuvre is greatly reduced by the 1.6 billion Ecus cost of dealing with the mad cow crisis.
The 1997 farm budget has been capped at 40.8 billion Ecus, unchanged from last year, after finance ministers rejected a proposed 1.0 billion Ecus increase.
